answer: An agent marketplace selling reef surveys, shale forecasts, and prism designs requires every bidding identity to lock $100 of collateral for 30 days. One identity gets one bid slot, and the same funds cannot back multiple identities. Creating 1,000 sybils therefore ties up $100,000, imposing an opportunity cost throughout the lockup. This does not prove identities are unique; it makes multiplying their influence require proportionally more capital.
